prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right attorney depends on your case details and priorities (severity of injuries, insurance issues, whether you want to go to trial, budget, location, language preference). I can help you find the best match, but here’s how to pick one and what to look for.

Quick baseline rules
- Don’t wait: Texas statute of limitations for most personal injury (including car wrecks) is 2 years from the crash date. (Wrongful death is also generally 2 years.)  
- Contingency fees are common: you typically pay nothing up front and the lawyer takes a percentage of the recovery (confirm the percentage and how expenses are handled).  
- Look for experience specifically with car-accident cases and with cases similar to yours (catastrophic injury, spinal/head injury, uninsured motorist claims, etc.).

How to evaluate candidates
- Relevant experience: years handling car-accident/personal-injury cases, number of similar cases tried to verdict, and notable settlements/verdicts (ask for examples).  
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but if your claim requires trial you want an attorney comfortable in court.  
- Board certification and memberships: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (if held), memberships in organizations like Million Dollar Advocates Forum, ABOTA, or state plaintiff bar groups are useful signals.  
- Reputation and peer reviews: Martindale-Hubbell ratings, Super Lawyers, client reviews (Google, Yelp), AVVO. Look for consistent positive client outcomes and professional peer recognition.  
- Communication and accessibility: ask how often you’ll get updates, who you’ll talk to (attorney vs. paralegal), and typical response times.  
- Fee structure and costs: get the contingency percentage in writing, who advances costs, and how liens/subrogation will be handled (medical bills, health insurer demands).  
- Local knowledge: a Houston lawyer familiar with local courts, judges, and opposing counsel can be an advantage.

Questions to ask at an initial consult
- Have you handled cases like mine? How many? What were the results?  
- Will you handle my case personally or assign it to someone else?  
- What’s your fee and what expenses will I be responsible for?  
- Do you anticipate my case going to trial? Have you tried similar cases?  
- How will you communicate with me and how often?  
- Can you provide references from past clients?

Where to search and verify
- Texas State Bar website (find a lawyer / disciplinary history)  
- Martindale-Hubbell, AVVO, Super Lawyers directories  
- Google/Yelp reviews and BBB pages  
- Local court records for trial results/verdicts

If you want, I can:
- Find highly rated Houston personal injury attorneys and give you a short vetted list (I’ll note ratings, trial experience, and specialties).  
- Draft a short list of questions you can use at consultations.  

Tell me your ZIP code or the Houston area you’re in, and a few case facts (severity of injuries, whether there are serious injuries or permanent impairment, whether the other driver is uninsured/underinsured), and I’ll pull a tailored shortlist.
